scope: The whitewashed Larabanga Mosque after restoration, around the 2010 Qualla publication. The exterior includes the tapered earthen buttresses, projecting timber torons, tall minaret and mihrab tower, and the small entrance with its patterned panel.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The national board describes the approximate 8m-square mud and timber mosque, its four entrances and adjacent baobab.
The University of Ghana inventory locates the mosque at latitude 9.2203 and longitude −1.86, in agreement with the named map object.
The conservation team restored the collapsed minaret and mihrab and replaced the harmful cement coat with traditional earthen plaster.
